To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
factoring spatial and spectral multchannel raw waveform CNNs into separate layers and incorporating MTL improves multichannel ASR performance.
factoring spatial and spectral operations and incorporating multi task learning improves the performance of multichannel CLDNNs.
factored spatial-spectral multichannel CLDNNs with MTL achieve 10% relative WER improvement over single channel models and 5% relative WER over unfactored multchannel models on a Voice Search task.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions.
how to factor multichannel raw waveforms into a series of operations that are jointly optimized with acoustic modeling.
how to best factor spatial and spectral multchannel raw waveform CNNs, and how to incorporate MTL into multichannel models.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
factoring and MTL are effective techniques for enhancing multichannel ASR, but they are not as powerful as the joint model from [1].
factoring the spatial and spectral operations in the network is better than not factoring them, and that incorporating MTL is also better than not incorporating it.
we can achieve a significant improvement in WER by factoring the spatial and spectral operations of the neural network and by incorporating MTL as a proxy for speech enhancement.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
factoring spatial and spectral multilevel processing is more effective than doing it in a single network layer, but MTL is not as effective as post-filtering.
we have achieved 20% relative improvement on a 2K hour task by combining factoring, MTL and multichannel training.
factoring the network and MTL is beneficial, but the benefits of MTL diminish with factoring.
The main takeaway from our work is that
factoring the spatial and spectral operations in the network is beneficial for multichannel ASR.
factoring multichannel operations into different layers in the neural network is beneficial for multichannel acoustic modeling.
factoring the network allows for more effective training and that MTL can be used as a proxy for speech enhancement.
